statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 12% (low), Stress 55% (elevated), Confidence 88% (high).
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping resolves to EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. A narrow evidence-based caution window is flagged from 12:30 UTC to 15:00 UTC covering the US data block, the cash open and ISM Services. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Compressed overnight NQ range and a VIX 15.20 close keep Tail low ahead of ISM Services and Friday payrolls
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed Sep 2 at 29,143.33, up 0.23%, in a 28,971.90-29,165.62 range, recovering after a three-day decline. Participation was broad: nine of eleven S&P 500 sectors advanced and the Russell 2000 added 1.13%. NVDA rose 3.21% on reporting of a Hugging Face acquisition valued near $14bn, while software groups lagged, so index leadership was narrow at the sector level but not one-directional. VIX fell 6.98% to 15.20 and closed at its session low. Overnight, NQ futures hold roughly 29,150, about 0.12% lower, within a 64-point two-way range, and ES futures span about ten points. That compression, with retracements functioning normally, is inconsistent with the persistent no-retracement path the Tail score measures, so Tail is low. Stress remains elevated on the macro and geopolitical backdrop rather than the price path. The 30-year Treasury yield reached its highest level since 2008 near 5.28% and the 10-year sits around 4.796% after easing from a three-year high, with NY Fed President Williams attributing the surge to economic strength and signalling a wait-and-see stance into the Sep 16 FOMC. US strikes on IRGC targets near the Strait of Hormuz on Sep 2 drew Iranian retaliation, with missiles intercepted over Kuwait, Jordan and Bahrain, and Hormuz transits reportedly falling from 23 to 10 vessels. WTI trades near $91 and Brent near $95. That unresolved conflict is a discontinuity risk in thin overnight liquidity rather than an observed trend mechanism. The scheduled path today runs through jobless claims, the trade balance and Fed Waller at 12:30 UTC, the cash open at 13:30 UTC and ISM Services at 14:00 UTC, with Fed Hammack at 19:00 UTC and payrolls on Sep 4.

lookbackSummary: Across the prior 24 UTC hours the published Claude path moved from a cautious European and pre-open stance to a progressively calmer one. Hours 00-11 UTC on Sep 2 carried Tail 20-23 with Stress 71-75, first in event/whipsaw mode and then trend-down through the European morning. From 12:00 UTC the assessment shifted to mixed mode as the US session produced an orderly broad-based rebound, with Tail falling from 18 to 11 and Stress from 68 to 54 by 22:00 UTC. Nineteen of the 24 hours have published assessments; hours 01, 16, 20, 21 and 23 UTC have none and are marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The forecast path assumes the compressed overnight range persists through the Asian session with Tail near 11-12, then drifts higher as European liquidity arrives and the US catalyst stack approaches. Conditional Tail crosses into the caution band only for the two hours spanning the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 14:00 UTC ISM Services print, where an opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks is the specific mechanism that would matter. It decays from 15:00 UTC on the assumption that price discovery is orderly and retracements occur, with a small nudge at 19:00 UTC for Fed Hammack. Stress stays in the elevated band throughout on long-end yields near multi-decade highs, the unresolved US-Iran conflict and pre-payrolls positioning. Confidence declines from 88 to 76 across the horizon as live price-path evidence ages.

forecast.analysis: Overnight NQ is holding a tight two-way range near 29,150 (about 64 points) after the Sep 2 cash close at 29,143.33 (+0.23%), with ES spanning roughly ten points. VIX closed at 15.20, down 6.98%. Observed mean reversion is functioning and no directional efficiency is present, so Tail sits low despite an elevated macro backdrop.
